You can make Patriots vs. Seahawks picks well before the kickoff on Sunday, Feb. 8, and it's fitting these are the only two teams left to make NFL bets on. That's because they boast the two best spread records this year, with Seattle at 14-5 and New England at 13-6-1. However, that also means they aren't making it easy to make 2026 Super Bowl predictions which such a small ATS margin between them. Seattle is favored by 4.5 points (O/U 45.5) per the latest Super Bowl odds from DraftKings Sportsbook, with that NFL spread tied for the largest in the Super Bowl over the last 15 years. Favorites of 4.5 points or more in the Super Bowl are 5-6, straight-up, since 2000. Underdogs have covered 52.6% of the time in Super Bowl history, which is close to the flip of a coin, so that Super Bowl spread trend may not help much with your Seahawks vs. Patriots bets. Top Super Bowl expert picks from Micah Roberts Roberts, a former Vegas bookmaker, is 11-4 (+658) over his last 15 Patriots ATS picks. For Super Bowl 60, Roberts is backing Seattle (-4.5) to cover. "The Patriots went 9-0 in away games, and the Seahawks went 8-1 in road games. Seattle won nine games in a row, with the last five games being against playoff teams and covering the last four. Drake Maye has looked shaky over the last few weeks, as has his offensive line. The Seahawks were No. 1 in the NFL against the rush number, 6th in total yards allowed (293.4), and No. 1 in total points (17.1) allowed. The real betting hasn't begun. I think this line moves through 5 and 5.5 quickly and closes 6." For Super Bowl LX, he is backing Seahawks RB Kenneth Walker III Under on rushing yard, which he locked in at 77.5 (-125). "New England's run defense is stout with the return of Milton Williams and I don't expect that to change in two weeks. Kenneth Walker is being asked to take on a bigger workload in the absence of Zach Charbonnet however we saw his effectiveness wane against the Rams as his touches increased, Walker is a dynamic playmaker and he'll be leaned into for sure although it might be more as a receiver than runner vs this Pats defense." He is backing the Under (45.5) in Patriots vs. Seahawks. "It is an outdoor game so maybe we get some elements in Santa Clara. But giving Mike Macdonald two weeks to prepare for sack- and fumble-prone Drake Maye makes me think Seattle will keep that New England offense in check. That offense did very little in the AFC title game. And I'm sure the Pats' defense will have some surprises for Sam Darnold , too. Our model has 44 points." articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. Based on Shough’s age and college profile, there is a possibility the market is overconfident in his abilities. Shough’s season passing total is currently lined within 200 yards of both Justin Herbert and Caleb Williams and 150 yards of Josh Allen , all quarterbacks with more NFL experience and a greater certainty that they will be starting in the league for seasons to come. Last season, Shough played against an extremely favorable slate of opposing defenses. Last year was considered a success for the rookie quarterback, but diving into the numbers raises some question marks for the Saints' passing attack. The Saints faced the 31st-ranked schedule of opposing passing defenses last season and are currently projected to face the 21st-ranked in 2026. In Shough’s nine starts, he faced one single team that finished the season with a winning record. Despite the soft schedule, the Saints dug themselves into early deficits, forcing Kellan Moore into heavier passing scripts. The Saints trailed at halftime in seven of nine games from Week 9 onward. In fact, the Saints led the league with the most offensive snaps while trailing. Although Shough wasn’t a complete garbage time merchant, he averaged 140 passing yards per game in the second half compared to 110 passing yards in the first half. An improved running game could help ease some of the need to rely on Shough as often as last year. The Saints finished 28th in total rushing yards and 31st in yards per rush in 2025 but were aggressive in signing running back Travis Etienne and guard David Edwards to help improve the run game. A better rushing attack can lead to a lower passing rate and create fewer clock stoppages, reducing Shough’s passing yardage ceiling. The Sharp Football season-long projections are more bullish on Shough compared to ESPN, but given the fragility of his profile, there is a good chance that Shough would need to start all 17 games to reach his season-long total. Last season, only 11 quarterbacks started 17 games, which provides a solid argument for betting season-long quarterback unders. In college, Shough did not start more than seven games in any of his first five seasons as he dealt with multiple different season-ending injuries. Betting overs on a sophomore quarterback, who was drafted after six seasons of college football, is probably not optimal. Given Shough’s injury history, there are probably multiple outs to cashing the under. DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid combined for 230 receiving yards, so Allen isn’t leaning on one target to move the offense. That makes Buffalo a tough team to slow down through the air. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to Tyler Shough in their opener. He went 35-of-56 with three touchdowns and two interceptions, and Detroit still escaped with a 31-30 overtime win. That yardage came on a heavy workload, and Allen doesn’t need anything close to it. He threw for 334 yards on 29 attempts, which is 27 fewer than Shough. A 220.5 target leaves plenty of room. and I'm back again with my weekly player props piece. Last season, I went 39-27 (59.1%) and 42-19 (68.9%) in 2024 for an overall success rate of 63.8% on my weekly props pieces. Let's get into my NFL player props for Week 2, including picks for Steelers vs Patriots , Seahawks vs Cardinals, and Dolphins vs 49ers. Download the Action Network app now for more picks and analysis! NFL Player Props — Week 2 Aaron Rodgers Under 0.5 Interceptions (-135 at bet365; -139 at DraftKings; -141 Caesars) Jeremiyah Love Longest Rush Under 11.5 Yards (-109 at DraftKings) Christian McCaffrey Under 43.5 Receiving Yards (-115 at bet365) Steelers vs Patriots Player Prop: Aaron Rodgers Interceptions I'm pretty shocked at this price given Rodgers hasn't been an interception machine at all in his career, even recently. Since he joined the Steelers, Rodgers has seven interceptions in 17 games, for a rate of 0.41 per game, throwing just 14 turnover-worthy plays (TWPs) in that time, which equates to pretty neutral interception luck since just north of 50% of TWPs are picked. That jives with my model, as he has a -0.18 per-game "gift" average compared to league average, so when he throws defended passes, they are ones that are still difficult to be picked, showing his elite ball placement. His matchup against New England is solid too. Last year the Patriots had 10 picks in 17 regular season games. Yes, they had four against Stroud in a playoff game, but it was clear Stroud was totally rattled in cold conditions. Overall, the Patriots ranked as a slightly below-average defense in passes defended and interceptions, and so far in 2026 they haven't shown anything to make me think much differently. My Luck Rankings Dashboard is showing Rodgers with a projected 0.44 interceptions and just a 35.7% chance of having one. That means this is good to around -180, but to be safe, I'd play this to just -150. Pick: Aaron Rodgers Under 0.5 Interceptions (-135) Seahawks vs Cardinals Player Prop: Jeremiyah Love Rush Yards In his NFL debut, Love had 11 carries for 41 yards with a long of 18 yards. That means, outside of that carry, he averaged 2.3 yards per carry against the Chargers, who were an explosive play machine against opposing RBs last year, ranking 25th in stopping explosive runs to running backs. Now he faces a Seahawks defense that dominates on the ground, ranking first last year. Yes, they allowed Rhamondre Stevenson to hit a long of 12 yards, but it took him 18 attempts to do so. Love is a fantastic talent, but the attempts likely aren't going to be there, as he had 11 in a heavily leading game script in Week 1. Despite Drew Lock being at QB for the Seahawks, I think this will be a more neutral-to-Seahawks-leading script, and it's reflected in Love's rushing attempt line as books have him at 10.5 attempts, heavily juiced to the under. Yes, I know Ty Okada is out, and Nick Emmanwori is questionable, but they were the same status in Week 1 and Seattle shut down Rhamondre Stevenson on what projects to be around eight more carries than Love should have. I'd play this to -130 or so. Picks: Jeremiyah Love Longest Rush Under 11.5 Yards (-109 at DraftKings) Dolphins vs 49ers Player Prop: Christian McCaffrey Receiving Yards When the 49ers are 9.5-point favorites or more (within a half point of a field goal plus a touchdown), McCaffrey has an average of 37.5 receiving yards, but a median of just 30.5 in twelve games on 4.8 targets per game. In those twelve games, he cleared 40.5 yards just four times, but in each of those four he went for more than 65 yards. Trim that to 12.5-point favorites (within a half point of a touchdown plus two field goals) and he averages 35.9 yards with a median of just 27 on 4.0 targets across seven games. Miami got gashed by Ashton Jeanty last week, but that was in a game with no Brock Bowers in a game that was close partway through the third quarter. San Francisco has so many more weapons and projects to be in a bigger blowout that there's enough opportunity to spread the ball around here that McCaffrey's receiving volume probably isn't going to be massive. After all, as I mentioned above, he's averaged just four targets in heavily favored games. I'm projecting a median in the mid 30s, but there's always a chance CMC has a 70+ yard receiving game like he's done in two of the seven games he's played as a 49er as a super-heavy favorite. However, those were the only two heavily favored games he cleared 40.5 receiving yards as a 49er. Based on his splits, he's likely to stay under, but if he clears it, you could do worse than throwing a sprinkle on 60+ or 70+ alt receiving yards.
